headline: Newport pier rebuild clears way for four Coast Guard cutters
dek: A $271.2 million contract covers the second phase of work on the storm-damaged Pier 1 at Naval Station Newport, with construction and cutter deliveries scheduled through 2030.
body: The Navy has awarded a $271.2 million contract for the second phase of rebuilding Pier 1 at Naval Station Newport, a project expected to provide four berths for Coast Guard cutters, according to an announcement from U.S. Sen. Jack Reed reported by What's Up Newp.

The original Coddington Cove pier was built in the mid-1950s, stretched about 1,585 feet and was condemned after years of storm and wave damage. The first phase of the project included demolishing the old structure.

The replacement will be roughly 1,000 feet long and 80 feet wide, with a higher deck intended to limit wave damage and account for sea-level rise. The contract also includes a new bulkhead, laydown area, parking, stormwater controls and utility work.

The Coast Guard has not announced which cutters will use the new berths. Construction and cutter deliveries are scheduled to continue through 2030, adding to a broader federal expansion at the Newport waterfront that includes a new NOAA marine operations center.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Newport Pier 1 rebuild gets $271.2 million Coast Guard contract
seoDescription: A $271.2 million Navy contract will rebuild Pier 1 at Naval Station Newport and provide four future berths for Coast Guard cutters.
